title: Get It Out, Do It, Put It Back
bigQuestion: When is a job really done?

story.title: The Block Corner Nobody Wanted
story.kicker: The tower was fun to build. The blocks on the floor were not fun at all.
paragraphs: Free time was over. Ms. Ruiz rang the bell. Sam and Ava had built a tall tower in the block corner. Now the blocks were all over the rug. Long ones. Short ones. Round ones.
Sam walked to the reading rug. Ava went to get a drink. Nobody looked at the blocks. Nobody wanted that job. The blocks just sat there.
Ms. Ruiz stood by the block bin. "You got the blocks out," she said. "You built with them. That is two parts. A job has three parts. What is the third?"
Sam looked at the empty bin. "Put them back," he said. Ava came over. They sorted the blocks by shape. Long ones in the front. Round ones in the back. The bin was full. Now the job was done.
story.think: Why did nobody want to put the blocks back? What made the job done?

lessons.title: Get It Out
lessons.mainIdea: Every job starts by getting out only what you need.
reading: Picture a box of crayons on a shelf. You want to color. You get the box. You get one sheet of paper. That is the first *part* of the job.
Get out only what you need. Do not dump the whole bin. If you need six blocks, take six. A big pile is hard to put back.
Look before you start. Is there room? Is the table clear? Now you are ready for part two.

words.d: one piece of a bigger job

look.title: The Crayon Box
look.text: Look at Leo. He wants to color one picture. He tips the whole crayon tub onto the table. Crayons roll off the edge. Two fall on the floor. He picks up a red one and starts to color.
look.prompt: What should Leo have done instead? What will be hard for him later?

check.q: What is the first part of every job?
check.why: A job starts by getting out what you need, and only that.

check.q: You need six blocks. What do you take?
check.why: Take only what you need. A big pile is hard to put back.

check.q: Why not dump the whole tub?
choices: A big pile is hard to put back
check.why: What comes out must go back. Less out means less to put away.

lessons.title: Do It
lessons.mainIdea: The middle part of a job is the work, and you finish the work before you stop.
reading: Now you color. Or build. Or set the table. This is part two. This is the *work*. It is the part people like best.
Do the work all the way. If you set the table, set every place. Do not stop at three plates when four people eat.
If you get stuck, ask. Say, "I need help with this part." Then keep going until the work is done.

words.d: the doing part of a job

look.title: Four Plates, Three Set
look.text: Look at the table. Four people will eat dinner. Nia set three plates, three forks and three cups. Then she saw her brother playing and went to join him. One chair has nothing in front of it.
look.prompt: Is the work done? What should Nia do before she plays?

check.q: Four people will eat. How many plates do you set?
choices: As many as you feel like
check.why: Do the work all the way. Every person gets a place.

check.q: You get stuck in the middle of a job. What do you do?
choices: Ask for help and keep going
check.why: Asking for help lets you finish the work.

check.q: Which part of a job is the work?
check.why: Get it out, do it, put it back. The work is the middle part.

lessons.title: Put It Back
lessons.mainIdea: A job is not done until everything is back where it belongs.
reading: You are done coloring. The picture is finished. But the crayons are on the table. Is the job *done*? Not yet.
Put the crayons in the box. Close the lid. Put the box on the shelf. Now the job is done. Now the table is ready for the next person.
This is the part people forget. It is the part that matters most. A job with no part three leaves a mess for someone else.

words.d: finished all the way, with everything put back

look.title: Is It Done?
look.text: Look at the art table. The painting is dry and pinned on the wall. The paint cups are still open. Two brushes sit in dirty water. The smock hangs off the back of a chair. The painter has gone outside to play.
look.prompt: Which part of this job is missing? Name three things that still need to happen.

check.q: Your picture is finished. Crayons are on the table. Is the job done?
choices: No, the crayons are not put back
Yes, someone else will clean up
check.why: A job is done when everything is back where it belongs.

check.q: Which part of a job do people forget most?
check.why: Put it back is the part people skip. It is the part that matters most.

check.q: What happens if you skip part three?
check.why: A mess left behind is a problem for the next person.

lessons.title: Bins, Hooks and Shelves
lessons.mainIdea: Everything has a home, and a home makes putting back easy.
reading: Look at a coat hook by the door. Look at a *bin* with a picture of blocks on it. Look at a shelf for books. Each one is a home for something.
When a thing has a home, putting it back is easy. You do not have to think. The coat goes on the hook. The blocks go in the bin.
When a thing has no home, it ends up on the floor. Then it gets lost or stepped on. A home keeps things safe.

words.d: a box or tub that holds one kind of thing
a curved holder on a wall for hanging things

look.title: Things With a Home
look.cite: example counts from one classroom corner
look.prompt: Which home holds the most things? Why is a bin better than the floor for forty blocks?

check.q: Where does a coat go when you come inside?
check.why: A hook is the coat's home. It stays clean and easy to find.

check.q: Why does a bin have a picture on it?
check.why: The picture tells you the bin's job, even if you cannot read yet.

check.q: What happens to a thing with no home?
choices: It ends up on the floor
check.why: Things with no home get dropped, lost or stepped on.

lessons.title: Sorting as You Go
lessons.mainIdea: Sorting things by kind makes putting away faster and finding them later easier.
reading: Picture a pile of toys. Cars, blocks and puzzle pieces all mixed up. Putting them away one by one is slow.
Try this. Pick one kind first. All the cars go in the car bin. Then all the blocks. Then the puzzle pieces. This is called *sorting*.
Sorting is faster. It also helps later. Next time you want a car, you know just where to look.

words.d: putting things in groups by kind

look.title: The Mixed-Up Pile
look.text: Look at the rug. There are five toy cars, ten blocks and twelve puzzle pieces in one big pile. Three bins sit nearby. One has a car picture. One has a block picture. One has a puzzle picture.
look.prompt: Which kind would you pick up first? How would you know when the whole pile is sorted?

check.q: Cars, blocks and puzzle pieces are in one pile. What is the fast way to put them away?
choices: One toy at a time, any order
Pick one kind at a time
Push the pile under the couch
check.why: Sorting by kind is faster than picking up one mixed thing at a time.

check.q: Why does sorting help later?
check.why: When each kind has its own bin, finding a toy is quick.

check.q: What does sorting mean?
choices: Putting things in groups by kind
check.why: Sorting is putting like things with like things.

sections.title: Jobs at Home and at School

lessons.title: Dishes, Clothes and a Bed
lessons.mainIdea: Home jobs like dishes, clothes and a bed follow the same three parts.
reading: After you eat, your *dish* is still on the table. Carry it to the sink with two hands. Scrape it if a grown-up shows you how. Now the table is clear.
Clean clothes go in the drawer. Dirty clothes go in the basket. Not on the floor. Not under the bed.
A bed is a job too. Pull the sheet up flat. Pull the blanket up. Put the pillow at the top. Three steps and it is done.

words.d: a plate, bowl or cup you eat or drink from

look.title: Making a Bed
look.text: Here are the steps for a bed, but they are mixed up. Put the pillow at the top. Pull the blanket up. Pull the sheet up flat.
look.prompt: Put the three steps in the right order. What would go wrong if you put the pillow on first?

check.q: Where do dirty clothes go?
check.why: The basket is the home for dirty clothes until wash day.

check.q: What is the first step in making a bed?
check.why: The sheet goes first, then the blanket, then the pillow.

check.q: How do you carry your dish to the sink?
choices: By sliding it across the floor
check.why: Two hands keep a dish from dropping and breaking.

lessons.title: The Helper Chart
lessons.mainIdea: A helper chart shows who does which job so nothing gets forgotten.
reading: Look at the wall by the classroom door. There is a *chart*. It has names and jobs. Line leader. Plant waterer. Table wiper.
A chart makes jobs fair. Everyone gets a turn. No one has to guess. You look, find your name, and do your job.
You can make one at home too. Feed the cat. Set the table. Put shoes by the door. Ask, "How can I help?" Then add it to the chart.

words.d: a list on the wall that shows who does what

look.title: Our Class Helper Chart
look.cite: example helper chart for one week
look.prompt: Which job needs the most helpers? Why might wiping tables need two people?

check.q: What does a helper chart show?
check.why: A chart lists names next to jobs so nothing is forgotten.

check.q: Why is a chart fair?
choices: Only the fastest kid gets a job
check.why: A chart gives each person a job and switches turns.

check.q: What can you say at home to find a job?
check.why: Asking how you can help is how you find a job and become a helper.

review.q: What are the three parts of every job?
choices: Get it out, do it, put it back
review.why: Every job has three parts. The last one is putting things back.

review.q: You built a tower. The blocks are on the rug. What is left?
choices: Put the blocks back in the bin
review.why: The job is not done until the blocks are back in their home.

review.q: You want one sheet of paper. What do you get out?
review.why: Get out only what you need. Less out means less to put back.
A hook is the coat's home. It keeps it clean and easy to find.

review.q: A pile has cars and blocks mixed up. What is the fast way to clean it?
choices: Pick up one toy at a time, any order
Sort by kind, one kind at a time
review.why: Sorting by kind is faster and helps you find toys later.

review.q: Which step comes last when making a bed?
review.why: Sheet, blanket, pillow. The pillow goes on last.
